hints: Focus on what excess $\text{LiAlH}_4$ actually does to a carboxylic acid, it is a very strong reducing agent.
Reduction of $\text{RCOOH}$ keeps the same carbon skeleton and gives $\text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$, so count carbons in P and Q carefully.
Check each pair for both the correct functional group in Q and the same total of 5 carbons as the starting $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$ acid.
walkthrough:
**Recall the reducing action of LiAlH4**

LiAlH4 is a powerful reducer. It reduces a carboxylic acid all the way to a primary alcohol.

General change:
$$\text{RCOOH} \xrightarrow{\text{excess LiAlH}_4} \text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Apply the carbon skeleton rule**

Reduction changes the $\text{-COOH}$ group into $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$. No carbon atoms are lost or gained.

So if P is $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$, then Q must also contain 5 carbons and must be a primary alcohol with the same alkyl group R.

**Test pair 1 and pair 2**

Pair 1 starts from $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{COOH}$ (pentanoic acid, C5). The correct product should be $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ (pentan-1-ol, C5).

The Q shown is $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{OH}$ which is butan-1-ol, only C4. One carbon is missing, so pair 1 is wrong. Pair 2 has the same wrong P, and its Q is $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{CHO}$, an aldehyde. LiAlH4 does not stop at the aldehyde, so pair 2 is wrong.

**Test pair 3 and conclude**

Pair 3 starts from $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCOOH}$ (2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid, C5). Changing $\text{-COOH}$ to $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ gives $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCH}_2\text{OH}$ (2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol).

This matches exactly, with the same branched skeleton and correct primary alcohol group. So only 3 is possible.

options.A: Incorrect. Pair 1 loses a carbon (C5 acid to C4 alcohol) and pair 2 gives an aldehyde. LiAlH4 with excess gives the primary alcohol with all 5 carbons retained, not these products.
options.B: Incorrect. Pair 3 is correct, but pair 1 is not. The Q in pair 1, $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{OH}$, has only 4 carbons while P has 5 carbons, so the skeleton has not been conserved.
options.C: Incorrect. Pair 3 is correct, but pair 2 is not. $\text{LiAlH}_4$ reduces $\text{RCOOH}$ fully to $\text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$, it does not stop at the aldehyde $\text{RCHO}$.
options.D: Correct. Only pair 3 works. $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCOOH}$ is a C5 acid and $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCH}_2\text{OH}$ is the corresponding C5 primary alcohol with the same branched alkyl group, exactly as expected for excess LiAlH4 reduction.
